source.title: Genome-Factory: An Integrated Library for Tuning, Deploying, and Interpreting Genomic Models
source.authors: Wei-Min Wu; Xue-Feng Song; Yi-Bo Wen; Qinjie Lin; Zhi-Han Zhou; Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu; Zhong Wang; Han Liu

page_placements.theme: Interpretable sparse dictionary features across model domains

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The title in the supplied metadata differs slightly from the title in the paper text; no other file problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses sparse autoencoders as an interpretability tool for genomic models and assumes they produce sparse, near-monosemantic latent units. Its reported results concern biological interpretation of those units, not whether superposition occurs or whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.
record.gate_note: The SAE analysis reports sequence-length associations, CTCF classification, and latent-dimension ablations. These concern genomic-model interpretability, but do not test superposition geometry, capacity pressure, feature overlap, or the completeness, stability, or canonicity of SAE features. Other reported benchmark and fine-tuning results do not bear on the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper is a software library for genomic foundation models. Its SAE module is used as an interpretability tool: SAE latents trained on DNABERT-2 embeddings are correlated with sequence length and probed for CTCF binding. The paper assumes SAE units are near-monosemantic and does not test superposition geometry, capacity pressure, or the completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features. The models are genomic, not LLMs, so V4 is not tested as stated. The SAE latents are not compared against neuron-level polysemanticity or distributedness.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors claim specific SAE latents encode sequence length and 'motif-centric regulatory features'. They also caution that the interpreter is 'an initial step', not a validated discovery tool. The headline conclusion of the paper is the library's usability across tuning, benchmarking and interpretation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an SAE trained on genomic-model embeddings and biological readouts; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method or measure its geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Three SAE latents (382, 519, 3519) on DNABERT-2 embeddings are reported as strongly correlated with sequence length; no values are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual SAE latents of genomic-model embeddings can track sequence-level properties such as length.

fits_no_version.finding: A logistic probe on SAE latents classifies CTCF-bound vs background sequences at 0.7881 accuracy. Zeroing the top latents lowers accuracy by roughly 0.02 each.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents of genomic-model embeddings carry information predictive of transcription-factor binding.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: For the SAE sequence-length findings, individual correlation values and uncertainty are not reported. The paper describes the interpreter as an initial step and says it is not a fully validated tool for biological discovery.

untested.parts: All parts: toy models, overlap geometry, sparsity transition.
All parts: capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
Distributed features or SAE-recoverable sparse features in LLMs. The study uses a genomic transformer and makes no neuron-vs-latent comparison.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicity of SAE features. The study only reports associations for selected latents.
All parts: whether superposed features are 1-D or multidimensional.

record.verdict_notes: The SAE section is a small demonstration within a software paper. No baselines are given: no raw-neuron or embedding probe and no random-latent ablation. The setup is inconsistent: Section 2.6 mentions GenomeOcean as an example model, while Section 3.3 uses DNABERT-2. The SAE layer, sparsity penalty and reconstruction quality are not reported. Benchmark and fine-tuning results are irrelevant to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model feature overlap, near-orthogonal geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure.
Whether LLMs spread features across neurons or have sparse features recoverable by a dictionary; the paper studies genomic models instead.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of a model's representation. The paper reports biological associations for SAE latents but does not test those properties.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: DNABERT-2
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlations between SAE latent activations and sequence-length labels.

conditions.value: 2,000 genome segments from Arabidopsis thaliana and Bos taurus; each segment 500–1,000 base pairs

rows.measure: Association of SAE latents with sequence length
rows.value: Latent 382, latent 519, and latent 3519 are described as exhibiting strong correlations; individual correlation values are not stated.
rows.locator: Section 3.3, Biological Interpretation of Genomic Models
rows.note: The paper reports these three latents together without separate correlation values.
rows.check: Selection-style result: three latents are named as strongly correlated, with no values, no baseline and no comparison to raw neurons. 'Observed' is not meaningful for any version.

rows.subject: DNABERT-2
rows.operation_detail: Trained logistic regression on SAE latent activations to classify CTCF-bound sequences versus background.

conditions.value: 39,024 total sequences; 20,000 ENCODE K562 CTCF-binding IDR peaks as positives and length-matched background sequences as negatives

rows.locator: Section 3.3, Biological Interpretation of Genomic Models
rows.note: The accuracy is for the logistic-regression probe on SAE latents.
rows.check: Probe accuracy on SAE latents with no baseline: no raw-embedding probe and no chance comparison are reported. It does not bear on any version.
